ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, shareholders, UBOs, and payment-rail counterparties against the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals List, the UN Security Council Consolidated List, the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and Panama's Lista de Sanciones Financieras (Ministry of Foreign Affairs). Politically exposed persons (PEPs) are subject to enhanced due diligence under Article 8 of Ley 23 de 2015, requiring senior management approval, source-of-funds documentation, and continuous monitoring; every screening event must be preserved in the AML case file.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá – Registro en Línea (https://www.registropublico.gob.pa/titulo/inicio/RegistroLinea)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be expressed in Spanish or transliterated into the Latin/Spanish script, must include the corporate designator 'S.A.' or 'Sociedad Anónima', and must be distinctive against the National Registry. Names in English or other languages may be accepted if they are not misleading and are transliterated into standard Spanish characters.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon official rejection, the applicant may within 48 hours file a written clarification with the Registro Público. If the rejection is maintained, the applicant must file an administrative reconsideration petition (recurso de reconsideración) with the Director of Registro Público within 5 business days of notification; a subsequent hierarchical appeal (recurso de apelación) must be submitted to the Sala Tercera de lo Contencioso-Administrativo of the Corte Suprema de Justicia within 10 business days from the second decision. All petitions may be prepared and stamped by a licensed attorney in Panama.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible. For a non-licensed UI/UX design subscription agency, Panama does not require physical occupation of the registered office. A virtual or co-working address may be used for service/billing purposes, but the licensed resident agent must maintain a separate physical office in Panama for receipt of process and regulatory correspondence; the registered office must be the address of the resident agent in Panama.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low but non-zero, estimated at 5% - 10% annually for non-financial businesses subject to the AML/CFT regime under Ley 23 de 2015; on-site visits are unannounced and conducted by the Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF) or the Public Registry's verification officers.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley 32 de 1927 (General Corporation Law of Panama), as amended, Articles 8, 12, 20, 47 and 53 (formation, capital and officers); complemented by Decreto Ejecutivo de Gabinete No. 45 de 26 de junio de 2019 (legalization of juridical persons) and Ley 2 de 14 de enero de 2011 (annual franchise tax / tasa única).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá (Public Registry of Panama) — Sección de Personas Jurídicas y Comerciales, Circuito de la Dirección Nacional de Registro.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura Pública No. ___ (Public Deed of Incorporation) containing the Pacto Social y Estatutos (Articles of Incorporation and Bylaws), registered with the Public Registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum authorized or paid-up capital; incorporation may proceed with nominal capital. No escrow account or capital deposit is required by Law 32 of 1927 for a standard Sociedad Anónima.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) that the subscription of [___] common shares of the Corporation by the initial subscribers be ratified, and the shares be declared validly issued, fully paid, and credited to stated capital; (2) that the registered office and the office of the resident agent be fixed at [address], Republic of Panama; (3) that [President], [Treasurer], and [Secretary] be appointed officers, each to serve until removed by the Board; and (4) that the President be and hereby is authorized to execute the Corporation's tax registrations, bank account documents, payment-aggregator agreements, and municipal licensing filings.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Search and Availability Certificate (Certificado de No Igualdad)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá — Ventanilla de Personas Jurídicas / Online Service Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an application with up to three proposed corporate names ending in 'S.A.' The Registry verifies absence of identical or confusingly similar registered names and issues the Certificado de No Igualdad, valid for 90 days, which is delivered to the notary together with the draft articles.
required_dossiers: Notarized application letter signed by the incorporating attorney
Copy of passport or cédula of each subscriber and director
List of up to three candidate corporate names
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a name is rejected as identical or confusingly similar, immediately file a fresh application with alternative names; the new certificate is issued within the same two-day SLA.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and Notarization of the Articles of Incorporation (Escritura Pública)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notario Público of the Republic of Panama (Notaría del Circuito of the incorporation domicile)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Pacto Social y Estatutos and execute before a licensed Panamanian Notary. The deed must state the corporate name, registered office, corporate purpose expressly covering UI/UX design and digital subscription services (ISIC 7410), authorized capital, identity of initial subscribers, board of directors, and the resident agent (abogado idóneo).
required_dossiers: Certificado de No Igualdad (name availability certificate)
Passport or cédula copies of all subscribers and directors
Proposed capital structure and share class provisions
Acceptance letter of the resident agent (resident agent's notarized consent)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Notarial defects are cured by a corrección notarial before registration; if discovered after inscription, file a public deed of amendment to correct the affected clauses.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Inscription of the Corporation with the Public Registry (Ficha)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá — Sección de Personas Jurídicas y Comerciales
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the notarized Escritura Pública and pay the official registration tariff (approximately USD 300 for authorized capital up to USD 10,000). Upon approval, the Registry issues the corporate 'Ficha' (registration card) and a Certificado de Registro evidencing the legal existence of the Sociedad Anónima.
required_dossiers: Original and two authenticated copies of the Escritura Pública
Municipal or bank receipt evidencing payment of the registry tariff
Certificado de No Igualdad
Resident agent sworn acceptance
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues a 'Razón' (query) or rejection, respond in writing within 10 business days with clarifications or an amended deed; an appeal lies to the Director General of the Public Registry against a final adverse ruling.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Taxpayer Registration (RUC) with the National Tax Authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas — Sede Electrónica / Regional Offices
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Access the DGI Sede Electrónica using the resident agent's credentials, complete Formulario de Inscripción del RUC with the Ficha data, tax domicile, and ISIC 7410 economic activity, attach the legal representatives' identification, and submit. The DGI issues the RUC certificate authorizing invoicing and tax compliance.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the Ficha (corporate registration record)
Certified copy of the Articles of Incorporation
Identification documents of legal representatives and directors
Proof of registered office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is rejected for inconsistent data, rectify the information in the Sede Electrónica and re-submit; no re-filing fee is charged for corrections made before approval.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Beneficial Ownership Registry Filing (Registro de Beneficiarios Finales)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) — Beneficial Ownership Registry Platform under Ley 5 de 2019 and its implementing regulations
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File in the official beneficial-ownership module each ultimate beneficial owner, namely any individual holding, directly or indirectly, 10% or more of the Corporation's capital, voting rights, or control. The resident agent files the initial return within 30 days following inscription; updates are filed when ownership changes.
required_dossiers: RUC certificate and corporate Ficha
Personal data forms and sworn declarations of each ultimate beneficial owner
Corporate organizational and ownership chart
Empowerment letter from the board to the resident agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Discrepancies are cured by filing a sworn corrective declaration before the competent authority; late filings attract statutory fines, therefore a prompt supplementary filing is the preferred remedy.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Aviso de Operación and Occupancy Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipio de Panamá (Dirección de Rentas Municipales) or municipality of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the Aviso de Operación by presenting the corporate documents, lease agreement, fire-safety certificate, sanitary clearance, and evidence of payment of the municipal fee computed from the declared activity (digital design services). The Municipality issues the Visto Bueno authorizing lawful physical operation of the office or studio.
required_dossiers: RUC certificate
Ficha and certified copy of the Articles of Incorporation
Lease agreement or property title for the premises
Certificado de Cuerpo de Bomberos (fire safety certification)
MINSA sanitary certificate for office premises
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Municipality queries the application, supply the outstanding documentation or request a reduced-premises classification; an appeal may be lodged with the municipal tax tribunal against any adverse assessment.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Settlement of Annual Franchise Tax (Tasa Única) and Go-Live
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Banco Nacional de Panamá / Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) Collection System
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Pay the flat annual franchise tax of USD 300 at Banco Nacional de Panamá or through the electronic platform, referencing the RUC, within 30 to 90 days of incorporation for the first period and, thereafter, by 15 March of each calendar year. Retain the payment receipt for the annual DGI compliance declaration.
required_dossiers: RUC number and corporate Ficha
Tasa Única official payment slip or electronic payment confirmation
Annual compliance declaration (if required by DGI)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late payment generates statutory penalties and interest; cure by immediate payment using the official surcharge sheet at Banco Nacional de Panamá or the DGI collection desk.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — ISIC 7410 (specialized UI/UX design and digital subscription agency) is an unregulated professional service under Panamanian law; no industrial or manufacturing license is required by the State.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Aviso de Operación (Municipal Operating Notice) — general municipal permit required for any physical office or studio; this is not an industry-specific statutory license and does not apply to a purely digital cross-border operation without physical premises.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt (Categoría I) — pure digital design subscription activity does not trigger a full Environmental Impact Assessment Study; an environmental registration is indicated only where a physical studio or office exceeds the size thresholds of Resolución AG-0473-2014.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater, VOC, or effluent discharge thresholds apply to digital design services. General obligations include proper municipal solid-waste disposal, electronic-waste management under MiAMBIENTE guidelines, and office noise limited to 65 dB(A) at the property boundary under MINSA standards.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Certificado de Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá (annual fire-safety certification covering emergency exits, extinguishers, and evacuation plans), municipal 'Visto Bueno' occupancy and structural inspection, MINSA sanitary clearance for office premises, and basic workplace-safety compliance under COPANIT standards applicable to computer-based office labor.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Republic of Panama operates without an issuing central bank. The Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP) is the prudential supervisor of the banking sector under Decree Law 9 of 1998, as amended by Law 21 of 2017. Banco Nacional de Panamá (BNP) acts as the fiscal agent of the national government and manages the dollarized monetary system. The United States Dollar (USD) is legal tender throughout the Republic pursuant to Law 84 of 1941; the Panamanian Balboa (PAB) is a nominal unit of account issued only as coinage at a fixed statutory parity of exactly 1:1 with the USD.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Panama is a fully dollarized jurisdiction with complete de jure and de facto convertibility on both the capital account and the current account. There are no exchange control statutes, no prior central-bank authorizations for capital movements, no surrender requirements, and no restrictions on dividend distributions, profit repatriation, intercompany loans, or service fee remittances. Under the territorial income tax model of the Código Fiscal de Panamá, a Sociedad Anónima deriving design subscription income exclusively from non-Panamanian clients and digital platforms is generally exempt from Panamanian income tax, provided the income lacks Panamanian source situs. Dividend distributions to non-resident shareholders are not subject to Panamanian withholding tax. The only compliance conditions precedent are: (i) maintaining an active Registered Agent; (ii) filing the annual Informe Anual with the Registro Público; (iii) paying the biennial corporate franchise tax; (iv) holding a valid RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyentes) issued by the Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI); and (v) filing Form P.F. 120 for the S.A. even where taxable income is nil. The use of Stripe Billing and Wise as settlement channels raises no convertibility obstacles because USD is the functional and reporting currency of the entity.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory export proceeds surrender, mandatory conversion ratio, or repatriation deadline exists in Panamanian law. Design subscription receipts in USD may be retained onshore or offshore indefinitely without any obligation to convert into Balboa coinage or receive any administrative endorsement. The absence of surrender rules is structural: since no national central bank issues paper Balboa currency and the USD circulates as legal tender, there is no regulatory mechanism or circular requiring conversion. In practice, the S.A. should preserve the MT103 credit notifications and payment-processor settlement reports to evidence the export of digital services in conformity with the territorial regime and to satisfy independent AML transactional monitoring.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: USD Operational Cash Account with Capital Contribution Verification Ledger
USD Operating Account paired with Merchant Settlement Sub-Ledger
USD Operating Account with Digital Banking API Access
USD Operating Account for Fintech and Cross-Border Digital Services
USD Institutional Operation Account; less suited to non-resident-owned digital service S.A.s

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: MEDIUM-HIGH. Panama has not enacted a dedicated Electronic Money Institution (EMI) licensing regime, so a fully indigenous Panamanian EMI license is unavailable. Cross-border EMIs such as Wise, Payoneer, and airwall-style clearing platforms may lawfully receive and settle design subscription funds for the benefit of the Panamanian S.A., because Panama imposes no exchange or payment-routing control. However, the S.A. must still maintain and disclose a domestic USD settlement account at an SBP-licensed bank as the compliance anchor and as the treasury concentration point. Wise Business is generally functional for collecting USD from US and UK subscription clients and onward-settling to a Panamanian account; Stripe Billing similarly settles in USD via Stripe's Panamanian acquirer arrangement or through US partner banks. The principal constraint is not legal permissibility but bank counsel's assessment: the domestic bank will consider the EMI a third-party processor requiring source-of-funds documentation and a processor agreement on file.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Pure remote account opening is available on only a limited exception basis. Under the Customer Due Diligence framework derived from Law 23 of 2015 (as amended), SBP regulations, and the beneficial ownership registry (Registro Único de Beneficiarios Finales), a natural-person signatory must generally attend an in-person or video-assisted interview with a designated compliance officer. In mainstream Tier-1 practice, at least one founding shareholder or appointed director is required to appear physically, or alternatively a Panamanian attorney-in-fact holding a notarized and apostilled power of attorney may complete the interview protocol. For a fully non-resident board, the accepted pattern is: (i) dispatche a copy of the public deed of incorporation, registered bylaws, and director resolution; (ii) deliver certified and apostilled passports plus bank reference letters from the shareholders' home banks; (iii) appoint a Panama-based resident agent and legal counsel; and (iv) schedule the interview for the designated representative. A limited number of banks (Towerbank, BAC, and certain boutique private banks) permit a video-interview modality with digital notarization where the final credit decision is confirmed with a physical visit to the representative office; this hybrid path is advisable for an ISIC 7410 design-agency entity domiciled outside Latin America.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Primary revenue arrives solely from overseas digital processors (Stripe Billing and Wise) rather than from traditional wire-instructed corporate clients.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide (i) the entity-matched processor verification screenshots for Stripe and Wise showing the exact legal name 'PA_CORP S.A.'; (ii) monthly processor settlement statements for at least three consecutive months; (iii) the published SaaS-style pricing page or subscription terms proving the Design-as-a-Service model; (iv) sample client invoices in USD; (v) a transaction-volume forecast letter prepared by the resident agent; and (vi) an organizational explanation memo describing why digital subscription rails are norm-based for ISIC 7410 services.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The beneficial owners are non-resident individuals resident in jurisdictions that the bank's internal jurisdiction risk model may classify as medium or high risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver (i) certified true copies of passports; (ii) tax identification or residence certificates from the shareholders' country of residence; (iii) a notarized CV or professional biography explaining the background in UI/UX product design; (iv) a portfolio of delivered design projects; (v) an organizational chart to the last individual; and (vi) the formal declaration submitted in the Panamanian ultimate beneficial ownership registry (RUP).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-frequency, low-ticket recurring sweeps from payment processors create velocity that may appear inconsistent with a small corporate treasury.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide (i) the SaaS contract master terms showing subscription billing cadence; (ii) export-ready subscription invoice logs from the billing system; (iii) reconciliation report aligning each processor payout with invoices numbers; (iv) chargeback and refund policy documents; (v) copies of customer engagement letters or statements of work; and (vi) read-only API access credentials to the upstream billing dashboard offered to the bank on a compliance viewing basis.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Absence of physical office and potentially low local substance for a territorial-taxed S.A.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Assemble (i) the resident agent service certificate; (ii) a serviced-office or virtual-office lease agreement in the Republic of Panama; (iii) a subscription to local bookkeeping or tax compliance representation; (iv) payment proof of the biennial corporation fee and the most recent annual report filing; (v) the DGI RUC certificate; and (vi) a substance memo describing where board decisions are executed, storage of records is centralized, and administration is conducted through the resident agent.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Post-settlement onward disbursement to overseas freelance designers and development sub-contractors may create a pass-through or money-transmitter perception.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Present (i) signed vendor/sub-contracting agreements including each contractor's identity and residence; (ii) deliverables-based evidence such as design asset handovers (Figma library exports, prototype files, source repositories); (iii) an invoice approval workflow chart; (iv) the treasury approval matrix of the S.A.; and (v) monthly payment batches exported from the accounting system, each mapped to the invoice and the bank MT103 outbound credit.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Equity injection from non-resident shareholders: execute a bank-to-bank SWIFT MT103 in USD to the S.A.'s USD account at the Panamanian bank, with remittance information stating 'Direct Investment – Equity Contribution to PA_CORP S.A.' and, where the bank requires, the BPM6 / IMF-based BOP component code for equity and investment fund shares (Direct Investment, Equity). Intra-group working capital advances must be routed under 'Other Investment' with a signed intercompany loan agreement, commercial-rate interest, and a board-approved resolution. Because Panama has no exchange control authority, no prior license or registration is required; the bank may, however, ask for the shareholders' contribution resolution and the updated RUC to substantiate the capital ledger. For design subscription proceeds, each Stripe or Wise payout should be consolidated in the same operating account, with the settlement report retained in the treasury file to evidence the commercial nature of receipts.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For outbound payments to overseas UI/UX contractors, the standard clearing rail is SWIFT MT103 over Panamanian correspondent banking relationships (typically Citibank N.A., JPMorgan Chase Bank, Bank of America, or Wells Fargo hub accounts in the United States). Payments clear in USD through Fedwire/CHIPS without exchange verification, as USD is the local monetary denomination. Commercial letters of credit are not required for the zero-inventory digital-services core; when physical design deliverables, hardware mockups, or procurement of third-party tooling is required, the S.A. may instruct a sight documentary credit under ICC UCP 600 through Banco General or Banistmo. All outbound treasury flows should carry the domestic PAN/ISO purpose narrative consistent with trade in digital design services to avoid misclassification by the beneficiary bank's AML filtering.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: USD-denominated money-market instruments at SBP-licensed banks (tier-one certificates of deposit and treasury repos) as liquidity buffer
EUR/USD deliverable forward contracts with global bank counterparties to hedge design subscription invoices denominated in euros
EUR/USD over-the-counter currency options under ISDA 2002 Master Agreement terms
USD/GBP cross-currency or deliverable forwards for UK-sourced subscription portfolios
Parallel or back-to-back intercompany set-off arrangements neutralizing multi-currency receivables without bank-market intervention
Non-deliverable forwards prohibited/irrelevant for PAB because the Balboa has no independently floating offshore market; all hedging must reference USD or third currencies
Currency swaps in EUR/USD or USD/GBP limited to tenors matching multi-year subscription enterprise agreements

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual franchise tax (Tasa Única Anual) payment and declaration — Ley 66 de 2010
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas, Panama
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually per last digit of RUC: 0-2 → March 15; 3-5 → April 15; 6-9 → May 15
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late settlement incurs a B/.50 penalty if paid by June 30 and B/.100 if paid after June 30; the S.A. is placed on the DGI default list (mora), good-standing certificates are withheld, and persistent non-payment across five fiscal years allows the Registro Público to strike off the entity administratively.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Municipal business patent (Patente Municipal) annual renewal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Municipalidad de Panamá (district municipality where the registered office is located)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within the first half of the fiscal year (calendar deadline: June 30 in Panama district); amount computed on 1% of qualifying gross revenue subject to a B/.50 statutory minimum tier
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 10% surcharge plus monthly interest (approximately 1% per month) on the unpaid balance; suspension of the operating patent and denial of municipal certificates until full settlement.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual beneficial ownership (UBO) confirmation filing under the Panamanian UBO Central Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección Nacional de Cumplimiento Financiero (DINCUFIN) — Registro de Beneficiarios Finales, Panama
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual confirmation aligned to the RUC-driven Tasa Única calendar (March 15–May 15) and any incremental update within 30 days after a shareholding or UBO change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Blocking of the DGI good-standing receipt and official certificates; administrative penalties for untimely or false UBO statements; repeated non-compliance is treated as a financial-compliance breach under Panama AML regulations.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A mandatory external audit is required when (i) gross annual income exceeds B/.1,000,000, requiring audited financial statements attached to the annual income tax declaration (Código Fiscal / DGI rules); (ii) the S.A. is a regulated financial, securities, insurance, or funds entity; or (iii) the company is listed on the Bolsa de Valores de Panamá. A UI/UX design subscription S.A. below the income threshold has no statutory audit obligation.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS (NIIF as adopted by Panama) governs the statutory financial statements; no separate local GAAP election exists — the DGI accepts IFRS-compliant balances under the territorial tax regime.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The S.A. must maintain a UBO schedule with the registered agent, listing every shareholder, director, and ultimate beneficial owner holding 25% or more of shares/control; the annual UBO confirmation and any transfer-triggered restatement are filed via DINCUFIN within 30 days of the change, with share transfers minuted and recorded in the share ledger; non-filing blocks good-standing certificates and the DGI annual tax receipt.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,500 – USD 6,000 for a certified audit engagement; USD 800 – USD 1,500 for a non-audit financial statement compilation (sufficient below the B/.1,000,000 audit threshold)

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general statutory tax holiday for a standard Panama Sociedad Anónima. A preferential 0-5% effective rate regime is available only for entities operating under the Multinational Headquarters (SEM) regime, Colon Free Zone licensed operators, or City of Knowledge technology operators satisfying economic substance requirements. Ordinary design-subscription revenue from Panama-source clients remains taxable at 25%; foreign-source revenue is outside the territorial tax net and no Panamanian effective tax rate applies.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 700 (Declaración de Renta) filed through the Panama Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) e-Tax 2.0 electronic portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual income tax return, supplemented by quarterly advance prepayment declarations for taxpayers exceeding the statutory gross-income threshold.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Annual return must be filed within three months after the close of the fiscal year; for a calendar-year entity, no later than 15 April following the fiscal year-end. Quarterly estimated payments are due on the statutory dates set by DGI during the active fiscal year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyentes), legal name, fiscal address, ISIC/NAICS activity code, and tax agent certification.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident sole shareholders need not enter a Panama NIT unless the company issues dividends to them; the company must provide the shareholder's country of residence and tax identification number of the ultimate beneficial owner.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: All gross revenue derived from services rendered, licenses, subscriptions, and digital design products consumed or economically used within Panama.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign-source subscription revenue (clients outside Panama, platform servers and management outside Panama) is excluded under the territorial regime. Claim exclusion in the reconciling schedule rather than omitting gross revenue entirely.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 - Cost of Sales and Direct Technical Costs
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Direct costs attributable to design services, freelance subcontractor fees, software licenses, cloud infrastructure, and internal labor directly used to generate Panama-source revenue.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Subject to transfer pricing rules if the cost is paid to a non-resident related party; unrelated foreign vendor invoices must be supported by properly validated e-invoices or equivalent documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: General administrative expenses, rent, employee salaries, statutory social security contributions, marketing, legal, accounting, and technology fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Expenses incurred wholly outside Panama or not benefitting the Panama operation may be disallowed if lacking economic substance. Deductions require invoices recognized by DGI and proof of bank routing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Separately discloses gross revenues from foreign jurisdictions, foreign taxes paid, and the statutory exclusion from Panamanian taxable base.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: To defend territoriality, maintain client contracts, IP licences, and evidence that decision-making and execution functions occurred in Panama. Avoid booking foreign subscription revenue as Panama-source.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 - Taxable Income and Applied Rate
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of net taxable income after statutory deductions and the application of the 25% corporate rate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The company with non-resident shareholders remains taxable on the Panama-source taxable income at 25%; no lower scale applies merely because shareholders are non-resident.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 7 - Advance Payments, Credits, and Retentions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Offsetting of quarterly advance income-tax payments, third-party withholding credits, and other statutory prepayments against annual CIT.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders cannot credit Panama CIT against their home-country tax; credits entered in this box belong exclusively to the Panamanian legal entity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 8 - Final Tax Payable or Refund Request
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net balance due or refundable after credits and prepayments; declaration includes Sarah? The line requires payment of the resulting Panama tax or a refund application.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Final payment must be wired in US Dollars from a Panamanian bank account or through authorized payment rails. Refund claims require complete fiscal documentation and are subject to DGI audit.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a surcharge equal to 10% of the tax due, plus monthly interest of 1% per month or fraction. Failure to file after formal notice may result in administrative fines between USD 50 and USD 500, suspension of the RUC, asset seizures, and criminal liability for fraudulent or reckless declarations.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before declaring a dividend from Panama-source profits, the paying corporation must obtain an approved dividend distribution voucher from the DGI. To invoke treaty relief, the non-resident shareholder must provide a Panama Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from its country of residence and submit the treaty relief application to the DGI together with the withholding tax return. If the shareholder is tax resident of a jurisdiction with a Panama DTA in force (e.g. Spain, Korea, Luxembourg, Mexico, Netherlands, Portugal, Qatar, Singapore, UAE or the United Kingdom), the applicable treaty rate may be reduced to 5% or 10%, provided the shareholder meets the beneficial-ownership and any limitation-of-benefits provision. Absent a DTA, the full 10% statutory WHT applies.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties for intellectual property used in Panama are subject to a statutory withholding rate of 12.5%; interest paid to foreign lenders is subject to 10% unless the payee is a recognized international banking institution and the loan is funded in the ordinary course of lending, in which case exemption may apply. Under DTAs, the reduced rates generally range from 0% to 10% for qualifying royalties and from 5% to 10% for financial interest. Foreign-source royalties and interest (economic use outside Panama) are outside Panama's territorial taxation and not subject to WHT.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Panama Balboa (PAB) 5,000,000 (USD-equivalent 5,000,000) in annual gross revenue triggers mandatory Transfer Pricing Documentation. Additionally, if controlled transactions with related parties exceed PAB 1,000,000, the taxpayers must prepare and maintain a Local File and Master File regardless of revenue threshold.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Panama's Economic Substance Regulations (ESR), enacted under Law 254 of 2021 and related implementing decrees, require a Panamanian entity engaged in relevant activities, including intellectual property exploitation and digital services, to demonstrate adequate physical offices, qualified staff, core income-generating activities, and local decision-making. For a UI/UX design-as-a-service subscription company, DGI scrutiny focuses on the substance of employees and strategy decisions in Panama; inadequate substance can cause recharacterization of income, denial of tax benefits, and a presumption that the entity is a shell company.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willful omission of Panama-source subscription revenue, fabrication of deductible expenses, false e-invoices, under-declaration of revenue from Panama-resident design clients, or artificial transfer of Panama-source income to offshore accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative penalty of 50-100% of the omitted tax, monthly late-payment interest, forfeiture of carried-over losses and deduction claims, and criminal conviction punishable by imprisonment for tax fraud under the Panama Penal Code and tax procedure rules.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, officers, and tax agents who sign false returns are jointly and severally liable for the omitted tax and penalties; civil restitution may include seizure of personal assets, travel bans, and disqualification from holding directorships; repeated violation mandates imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a Panamanian Sociedad Anónima that merely nominally holds subscription contracts or IP without physical presence, employees, management, or local bank accounts, and claiming territorial advantages without genuine activity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty benefits, recharacterization of profits as Panama-source, application of the 25% CIT with penal interest, cancellation of economic substance registration, strike-off of the entity from the Public Registry, and additional fines under the ESR legal framework.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face personal liability where the company is a façade; the judicial authority may pierce the corporate veil, impose civil restitution equal to the profits routed abroad, issue personal travel bans, and pursue criminal charges of fraud or aggravated tax evasion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Anti-Money Laundering Deficiency and Illegal Financial Flows
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to conduct customer due diligence on subscription clients, accepting funds from sanctioned jurisdictions without AML screening, using nominee or bearer shares to conceal beneficial ownership, or executing transactions through unauthorized financial channels.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines from USD 10,000 to USD 1,000,000 per violation, suspension of the RUC, prohibition against conducting financial transactions, confiscation of proceeds, and criminal prosecution for money laundering under Panama's AML/CFT regime.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Compliance officers and directors may be held criminally liable and face imprisonment of up to 12 years, personal monetary fines, seizure of personal estates, travel restrictions, and barring from serving regulated financial or corporate positions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to file contemporaneous Local File/Master File after exceeding thresholds, refusing to provide benchmarking studies, transacting with related non-resident entities above arm's length, or submitting inconsistent TP documentation after the statutory deadline.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Mandatory adjustment of taxable income by the benefit-derived amount, administrative penalty equal to 25-50% of the adjusted tax differential, late payment interest, restriction of refund claims, and publication of the taxpayer in the DGI non-compliance register.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign incomplete TP disclosures are subject to joint liability for the corrected tax, civil damages for misrepresentation, travel bans pending resolution, and in aggravated cases, criminal prosecution for false documentation in tax procedures.
